newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK BANK SAYS MULLS FIRST SYND LOAN.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK BANK SAYS MULLS FIRST SYND LOAN.

text.p: Slovenska Sporitelna a.s., Slovakia's largest savings bank, said on Tuesday it was mulling its first forray into the international syndicated loan market for 1997, in an attempt to establish the bank abroad.

"The aim of the (first) syndicated loan is to enter the international market with a smaller volume and establish there, and from the obtained funds cover further similar activities," Sporitelna Treasury Director, Ivan Benda, told Reuters.

Benda said it was still too early to discuss possible terms of the loan or its length, but added: "It would be pointless to start with $100 million right away...(because) you never get the best price right away".
One bank official, who requested anonymity, said that a volume of around $50 million may be more suitable for the bank's first foreign loan.

Benda said that Sporitelna was already recognised on international markets, given the bank's monthly traded volumes on the foreign exchange market of about $3 billion, and $2 billion on the money market, but the loan would further heighten its exposure.
Last Friday, Moody's Investors Service assigned Sporitelna ratings of Ba1 for long-term deposits, Not Prime for short-term deposits, and D for bank financial strength.
According to Moody's, Sporitelna's ratings reflect the bank's "improving, but moderate" capitalisation, and the limited scale of its lending operations.
Sporitelna accounts for 45 percent of the country's deposit market, holds a high share of loans and dominates the retail banking sector.

"Soon it will be clear how we will use the rating, to receive it was only the first step," Benda said. "But currently we have no need for a bond issue, as we are very strong in primary deposits," he added.
